primary.old: Must be responsible for arranging or paying for a funeral.
primary.new: You or your partner must be responsible for the funeral costs.
primary.reason: Replace “arranging or paying” with responsibility for costs.

evidence.claim: The applicant or their partner must be responsible for the funeral costs.
evidence.quote: you or your partner are responsible for the funeral costs
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

evidence.claim: Responsibility for arranging the funeral by itself is sufficient.
evidence.quote: the client or their partner is responsible for the cost of the funeral
evidence.judgeNote: The source requires responsibility for the costs, not merely arranging the funeral.

primary.old: Letter of compliance to The Pensions Regulator (declaration of compliance within 5 months of duties start date)
primary.new: Declaration of compliance to The Pensions Regulator within five calendar months after the duties start date.
primary.reason: The employer submits a declaration, not a letter.

evidence.claim: Employers must send a letter of compliance to The Pensions Regulator.
evidence.quote: You must complete your declaration of compliance to tell us how you have met your legal duties.
evidence.judgeNote: The required submission is a declaration of compliance; the regulator sends the employer a letter with a code.

evidence.claim: The declaration of compliance must be completed within five months of the duties start date.
evidence.quote: You must complete your declaration with The Pensions Regulator within five calendar months after your duties start date.
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

primary.old: Available to anyone who has received a decision from HMRC (on income tax, VAT, PAYE, penalties, etc.) and disagrees with it. Must appeal within 30 days of the HMRC review conclusion. No filing fee for most tax appeals.
primary.new: You can appeal some HMRC tax decisions and penalties to the First-tier Tribunal. For direct tax, you must usually appeal to HMRC first. The tribunal appeal deadline is usually 30 days from the relevant decision or review conclusion. There is no fee to appeal.
primary.reason: Qualify the decisions and the deadline trigger.

evidence.claim: Anyone who disagrees with any HMRC decision can appeal to the tax tribunal.
evidence.quote: You can appeal to the First-tier Tribunal (Tax) if you want to challenge some decisions by: HM Revenue and Customs ( HMRC )
evidence.judgeNote: The tribunal accepts some HMRC decisions, not every HMRC decision; direct tax cases must first be appealed to HMRC.

evidence.claim: Income Tax, VAT and PAYE decisions can be appealed.
evidence.quote: Direct tax includes: Income Tax PAYE Tax Corporation Tax Capital Gains Tax National Insurance contributions Inheritance Tax Indirect tax includes: VAT
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

evidence.claim: Some HMRC penalties can be appealed.
evidence.quote: You may be able to appeal if HMRC : sends you an assessment for duty charges you a penalty
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

evidence.claim: An appeal following an HMRC review conclusion must be made within 30 days.
evidence.quote: The time limit is 30 days from: the view of the matter letter – direct tax the assessment or decision – indirect tax a review conclusion letter – either indirect or direct tax
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

evidence.claim: There is no filing fee for most tax tribunal appeals.
evidence.quote: There is no fee for appealing to the First-tier Tribunal.
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

primary.old: Mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses — must keep digital records and file VAT returns via MTD-compatible software. Income Tax MTD rolls out from April 2026 for self-employed/landlords with income over £50k.
primary.new: VAT-registered businesses must use Making Tax Digital for VAT unless exempt or applying for an exemption; they keep digital VAT records and submit returns using compatible software. Making Tax Digital for Income Tax began on 6 April 2026 for qualifying sole traders and landlords whose 2024 to 2025 qualifying income was over £50,000.
primary.reason: Add the VAT exemption and use the current Income Tax start date and qualifying-income basis.

evidence.claim: Making Tax Digital for VAT is mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses.
evidence.quote: All VAT registered businesses should now be signed up for Making Tax Digital for VAT unless you’re exempt or have applied for exemption.
evidence.judgeNote: Exempt businesses and those applying for an exemption are exceptions to the universal claim.

evidence.claim: VAT businesses covered by Making Tax Digital must keep digital VAT records.
evidence.quote: You should now keep VAT records and submit VAT Returns using compatible software.
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

evidence.claim: VAT businesses covered by Making Tax Digital must submit VAT returns through compatible software.
evidence.quote: You should now keep VAT records and submit VAT Returns using compatible software.
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

evidence.claim: Making Tax Digital for Income Tax begins in April 2026 for qualifying sole traders and landlords.
evidence.quote: From 6 April 2026, sole traders and landlords must use it if their total annual income from self-employment and property is over £50,000.
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

evidence.claim: The Income Tax threshold is more than £50,000 of self-employment or property income.
evidence.quote: have qualifying income of more than £50,000 — read more about what qualifying income is and what is included
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

primary.old: Free to use for any business or organisation looking to supply goods or services to the public sector. Contracts above £12,000 (central government) or £25,000 (other public bodies) must be published here.
primary.new: Contracts Finder is free to use to search public contract opportunities. It remains in use for in-scope procurements begun under the previous regulations before 24 February 2025; new procurements under the Procurement Act 2023 are published on Find a Tender.
primary.reason: The old publication thresholds omitted the procurement regime transition.

evidence.claim: Contracts Finder is free to use.
evidence.quote: Contracts Finder is free to use.
evidence.judgeNote: The guidance explicitly says it is free.

evidence.claim: Any business or organisation can use Contracts Finder to seek public sector supply opportunities.
evidence.quote: You can use Contracts Finder to: search for contract opportunities in different sectors
evidence.judgeNote: The text describes searching opportunities but does not explicitly establish access for every business or organisation.

evidence.claim: Central government contracts above £12,000 must be published on Contracts Finder.
evidence.quote: central government authorities [footnote 3] , where the contract value is at least £12,000 [footnote 4] inclusive of VAT;
evidence.judgeNote: The £12,000 threshold is stated, but publication duties are limited to in-scope procurements and may have exemptions.

evidence.claim: Contracts above £25,000 from other public bodies must be published on Contracts Finder.
evidence.quote: sub-central contracting authorities, NHS Trusts and NHS Foundation Trusts where the contract value is at least £30,000 [footnote 5] inclusive of VAT.
evidence.judgeNote: The stated threshold for these other authorities is £30,000 including VAT, not £25,000.

evidence.claim: Current scope check
evidence.quote: This guidance only applies to procurements commenced before 24 February 2025 under the PCRs.
evidence.judgeNote: Seen on current official page; fetcher must confirm the literal span before application.

evidence.claim: Current scope check
evidence.quote: Any procurements whether above or below threshold commenced from 24 February 2025 only require notices to be published on FTS.
evidence.judgeNote: Seen on current official page; fetcher must confirm the literal span before application.

primary.old: Required for any charitable collection in a public street or place in England and Wales. Free to obtain. Greater London collections (outside City of London) go through the Metropolitan Police. Penalty: £200 fine for collecting without a licence.
primary.new: You might need a licence to collect money or sell items for charity on the street, depending on the local council. In Greater London outside the City of London, contact the Metropolitan Police. You could be fined £200 for collecting money for charity without a required licence.
primary.reason: Remove the unsupported free claim and qualify when a licence is needed.

evidence.claim: Every charitable collection in a public street or place in England and Wales needs a street collection licence.
evidence.quote: If you want to collect money or sell items on the street for charity, you might need a street collection licence, depending on your local council.
evidence.judgeNote: The page says a licence might be needed depending on the council, rather than for every collection.

evidence.claim: Greater London collections outside the City of London go through the Metropolitan Police.
evidence.quote: In Greater London (except the City of London) you’ll need to contact the Metropolitan Police for a licence.
evidence.judgeNote: The source identifies the Metropolitan Police route and the City of London exception.

evidence.claim: Collecting for charity without a licence can lead to a £200 fine.
evidence.quote: You could be fined £200 if you collect money for charity without a licence.
evidence.judgeNote: The source states the possible £200 fine.

primary.old: Must have reached State Pension age (66 or over).
primary.new: Must have reached State Pension age.
primary.reason: Use the date-of-birth State Pension age test rather than 66.

evidence.claim: An applicant must have reached State Pension age.
evidence.quote: You can get Attendance Allowance if you’ve reached State Pension age and the following apply:
evidence.judgeNote: The source makes reaching State Pension age an eligibility condition.

evidence.claim: Being 66 or over meets the Attendance Allowance age condition.
evidence.quote: The State Pension age for men and women will now increase to 67 between 2026 and 2028.
evidence.judgeNote: State Pension age is rising above 66, so being 66 is not always enough.

primary.old: A registered LPA exists and the donor has died.
primary.new: A registered LPA existed and its donor has died; the donor’s death must be reported to the Office of the Public Guardian.
primary.reason: Clarify this node is about reporting a donor’s death, not starting to use an LPA.

evidence.claim: A registered LPA must exist to use the LPA service.
evidence.quote: You must have registered the LPA before you can start acting as an attorney.
evidence.judgeNote: The source requires registration first.

evidence.claim: The donor has died when the LPA is activated or used.
evidence.quote: OPG will cancel the LPA if the donor dies
evidence.judgeNote: The source says the LPA is cancelled on the donor’s death rather than activated or used then.

evidence.claim: Current scope check
evidence.quote: You must tell the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) if:
evidence.judgeNote: Seen on current official page; fetcher must confirm the literal span before application.

evidence.claim: Current scope check
evidence.quote: the donor, or another attorney, dies
evidence.judgeNote: Seen on current official page; fetcher must confirm the literal span before application.

primary.old: Must have reached State Pension age (currently 66).
primary.new: If you are single, you must have reached State Pension age. If you have a partner, you may qualify if both of you have reached State Pension age or one of you gets Housing Benefit for people over State Pension age.
primary.reason: Remove fixed age and include the mixed-age couple exception; requires a matching rule decision.

evidence.claim: A Pension Credit claimant must have reached State Pension age.
evidence.quote: You’ll be eligible if either: you and your partner have both reached State Pension age one of you is getting Housing Benefit for people over State Pension age
evidence.judgeNote: The general age rule has a mixed-age couple exception when one partner gets Housing Benefit for people over State Pension age.

evidence.claim: State Pension age is currently 66.
evidence.quote: The State Pension age for men and women will now increase to 67 between 2026 and 2028.
evidence.judgeNote: The age is rising in stages during 2026–2028, so it is not uniformly 66 now.

primary.old: Must have reached State Pension age (currently 66). Some disabled people may also qualify before this age.
primary.new: In England, you can get an older person’s bus pass when you reach State Pension age. An eligible disabled person may qualify for a separate disabled person’s pass.
primary.reason: Scope the current node to England; the age-60 routes in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland require separate treatment.

evidence.claim: An older person must have reached State Pension age to get a bus pass.
evidence.quote: In Wales you can get a bus pass when you reach 60.
evidence.judgeNote: The State Pension age rule applies in England, while Wales allows the pass at 60 and Scotland and Northern Ireland also use 60.

evidence.claim: State Pension age is currently 66.
evidence.quote: The State Pension age for men and women will now increase to 67 between 2026 and 2028.
evidence.judgeNote: The age is rising in stages during 2026–2028, so it is not uniformly 66 now.

evidence.claim: Some disabled people can qualify for a bus pass before reaching the older-person qualifying age.
evidence.quote: You’re eligible for a disabled person’s pass if you live in England and are ‘eligible disabled’.
evidence.judgeNote: The source confirms a disabled-person route but does not expressly state that it is available before the older-person qualifying age.

primary.old: The funeral must take place in the UK, and applicant must live in Scotland.
primary.new: You must live in Scotland. The funeral may be held in the UK or, in some circumstances, another country.
primary.reason: The funeral need not always be in the UK.

evidence.claim: The funeral must take place in the UK.
evidence.quote: the funeral is being held in the UK or in some circumstances , another country
evidence.judgeNote: The source allows a funeral in another country in some circumstances.

evidence.claim: The applicant must live in Scotland.
evidence.quote: you live in Scotland
evidence.judgeNote: Supported by the cited source.

primary.old: Must have been under State Pension age (66) at the time of the partner's death.
primary.new: You must have been under State Pension age when your partner died.
primary.reason: Use State Pension age, not fixed 66.

evidence.claim: The claimant must have been under State Pension age when their partner died.
evidence.quote: When your partner died, you must have been: under State Pension age
evidence.judgeNote: The source states the timing and age requirement.

evidence.claim: State Pension age is currently 66.
evidence.quote: The State Pension age for men and women will now increase to 67 between 2026 and 2028.
evidence.judgeNote: The age varies by date of birth during the 2026–2028 transition and is not fixed at 66.

primary.old: A person has died in England or Wales.
primary.new: For this local register-office process, the death occurred in England or Wales.
primary.reason: Clarify this node covers the England and Wales process; the broad GOV.UK landing page links to other processes.

evidence.claim: The death must have happened in England or Wales to use the death-registration guidance.
evidence.quote: Find out how to register a death in the UK or abroad.
evidence.judgeNote: The source includes deaths elsewhere in the UK and abroad, so England or Wales is not a universal condition.

evidence.claim: Current scope check
evidence.quote: death certification reform, England and Wales
evidence.judgeNote: Seen on current official page; fetcher must confirm the literal span before application.

evidence.claim: Current scope check
evidence.quote: By law, deaths must be registered within 5 days of receipt of the MCCD
evidence.judgeNote: Seen on current official page; fetcher must confirm the literal span before application.

primary.old: Adults aged 18 and over must attend in person. Children under 18 can be included on a parent's ceremony.
primary.new: Adults aged 18 or over who successfully applied for British citizenship usually need to attend a ceremony; people who become citizens under the Windrush scheme may choose whether to attend. Children under 18 who applied with their parents may attend a parent’s ceremony.
primary.reason: Add the Windrush exception and qualify the child route.

evidence.claim: Every applicant aged 18 or over must attend a citizenship ceremony.
evidence.quote: If you become a British citizen under the Windrush scheme you can choose if you want to attend a citizenship ceremony.
evidence.judgeNote: The source makes attendance optional for the Windrush scheme and also lists citizenship categories that do not require a ceremony.

evidence.claim: People who attend a citizenship ceremony attend it in person.
evidence.quote: You must take your invitation when you go to your ceremony.
evidence.judgeNote: The source describes going to the ceremony with the invitation.

evidence.claim: A child under 18 who applied with their parents may attend a parent’s citizenship ceremony.
evidence.quote: Children under 18 who have applied with their parents may attend a ceremony with other members of the family, to collect their certificate.
evidence.judgeNote: The source expressly allows children to attend with family.
